guide.mtgcard.card_database.p_overview: The Card Database is your personal card vault. It stores the MTG cards you’ve collected, like an ender chest — each player has their own separate storage.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_personal: Each player gets their own Card Database inventory.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_cards_only: Only MTG Cards can be stored from your inventory into the database.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.p_deckbox: If a Deckbox is placed directly next to the Card Database, an extra Deckbox panel appears on the right. You can move cards between your vault and the selected deckbox tab.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_adjacent: Deckboxes must be touching the Card Database (any side).
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_tabs: If multiple deckboxes are adjacent, use the tab buttons to pick which deckbox you’re viewing.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_tab_names: Tabs can show commander/partner names if they’re set in the deckbox’s side slots.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_store_all: ⇪ Store All: moves every MTG Card from your inventory + hotbar into the database.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_sort: S Sort: changes how cards are ordered (Name, Mana Value, Price, Type, P/T, Rarity).
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_route: P/D Route: controls where shift-clicked cards from the top window go: P = Player inventory, D = Deckbox.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_from_db: Shift-click a card in the top 6×9 window to move it out. It will go to your inventory (P) or into the active deckbox (D).
guide.mtgcard.card_database.b_to_db: Shift-click a card in your inventory to store it into the database.
guide.mtgcard.card_database.p_search: Use the search bar to filter what’s shown in the top 6×9 window. Results update automatically as you type. Sorting also applies to searches.
guide.mtgcard.card.title: Card
guide.mtgcard.card.p_overview: Cards can be viewed full-screen, tracked with counters, and displayed in the world.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_open_view: Right-click to open the large view.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_info: Press Tab (or click the i) to open the info panel.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_rotate: Press E (or right-click the card) to rotate 90°.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_flip: Double-faced cards: press R (or use the flip button) to switch faces.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_facedown: Use the Facedown toggle to hide/reveal the card.
guide.mtgcard.card.p_counters: Counters are saved on the card and can be adjusted from the HUD or the Counters tab.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_hud: If counters exist, a mini HUD appears on the right.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_adjust: Use +/- or scroll over a counter to change its value.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_editor: Create counters by typing a name, choosing an icon, then pressing Create.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_place: Sneak + right-click a block face to place the card as a display.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_air: Sneak + right-click opens the large view instead of placing.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_display_interact: Right-click the display to rotate; sneak-right-click to open the large view.
guide.mtgcard.card.b_display_break: Breaking the display drops the stored card.
guide.mtgcard.pack.title: Pack
guide.mtgcard.pack.p_overview: Packs open into a 15-card bundle, with progress shown on-screen while cards are generated.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_use: Right-click a pack to open it.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_lock: You can only open one pack at a time.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_hud: A progress HUD appears while the pack is opening.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_bundle: When finished, you receive a Bundle containing the cards.
guide.mtgcard.pack.p_set_codes: The pack can target a specific set based on its display name (or stored data).
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_brackets: Name the pack like "[mh3]" (2–6 characters) to lock the set.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_bare: You can also name it "mh3" (no brackets) or "custom".
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_data_fallback: If no name is found, the pack may use its internal data tag.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_recipe: A pack contains 15 slots: 6 commons, 1 wildcard (C/U), 3 uncommons, 1 basic land, 1 foil slot, 1 rare/mythic, 1 token/art, and 1 random slot.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_foil_slot: The foil slot is always given a glint effect.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_token_slot: The token/art slot is the only slot allowed to contain token-like items.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_no_dupes: The pack tries to avoid duplicates while generating cards.
guide.mtgcard.pack.p_custom: Custom behavior depends on the pack’s name.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_custom_unnamed: Unnamed packs may roll a per-slot chance to pull from the global custom pool (config-based).
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_custom_force: If named "custom", the pack always tries custom cards first, then falls back to normal pulls if needed.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_custom_set_force: If named with a custom set code, the pack will force that custom set first.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_official_set_lock: Official set packs are set-locked for all non-token slots.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_refund: If pack generation fails, the pack attempts to refund the exact consumed pack.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_creative: In Creative mode, packs are not consumed.
guide.mtgcard.pack.b_sound: Opening a pack plays a UI sound.
guide.mtgcard.dice.title: Dice
guide.mtgcard.dice.p_overview: Dice allow quick, shared random rolls that are announced to nearby players.
guide.mtgcard.dice.b_right_click: Right-click a dice item to roll it.
guide.mtgcard.dice.b_stack_count: The number of dice rolled equals the stack size (for example, 3 dice = 3dX).
guide.mtgcard.dice.b_result: The total result is shown at the end of the roll.
guide.mtgcard.dice.b_sneak: Sneak while rolling to reveal individual roll results.
guide.mtgcard.dice.b_individual_rolls: Individual rolls are shown in brackets before the final total.
guide.mtgcard.dice.b_range: Roll results are sent to players within 50 blocks.
guide.mtgcard.dice.b_dimension: Only players in the same dimension will receive the message.
guide.mtgcard.dice.b_chat: Rolls are announced in chat with the player name and dice type.
guide.mtgcard.dice.p_types: The mod includes multiple dice sizes such as D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D20, and D100.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.title: Deckbox
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.p_overview: The Deckbox is a dedicated storage block for MTG cards, with special slots for deck essentials and shulker-like drops that preserve contents.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_open_right_click: Right-click the Deckbox to open its storage UI.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_open_state: The block visually opens while at least one player has it open.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_waterloggable: Deckboxes can be placed in water (waterloggable).
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_main_grid: Main storage is an 11×9 grid (99 slots).
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_cards_only: The main grid only accepts MTG cards.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_side_slots: There are 3 side slots for deck-related items.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_bundle_slot: Top side slot: Bundle-only (for holding a packed group of cards).
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_quick_move_cards: Shift-clicking a card tries the main grid first, then the commander/partner slots.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_quick_move_bundl: Shift-clicking a bundle inserts it into the bundle slot.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_quick_move_block: Non-card items (and non-bundles) are blocked from inserting.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_dye_any_hand: Use a dye on the Deckbox to change its tint (checks both hands).
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_consumes_dye: Dye is consumed unless you are in Creative mode.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_tint_bar: The Deckbox UI shows a small tinted accent bar matching the current color.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_keeps_contents: When broken, the Deckbox drops as an item that keeps its contents inside.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_picks_up_tint: Tint color is saved and restored when placed again.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_creative_break: Breaking in Creative still produces a single saved Deckbox item (prevents spilling/duplication).
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_comparator_main_: Comparators read only the main 99 slots (not the side slots).
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_comparator_scale: Comparator output scales from 0–15 based on how full the main grid is.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.b_deck_control_not: Updating the Deckbox notifies adjacent Deck Control blocks automatically.
guide.mtgcard.deckbox.p_preview: Hover over a card slot to preview the card art. Foil cards show a subtle shimmer effect in the preview.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.title: Deck Control
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.what_is.title: What it is
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.what_is.body: Deck Control is a deck operator block for your Deckbox. It lets you draw, shuffle, peek, scry, surveil, mill, cascade, and place cards back into the library without opening the Deckbox inventory.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.linking.title: Linking
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.linking.bulle: Place a Deckbox adjacent (any side). The Deck Control will link to the first Deckbox it finds.
Once linked, it locks to that Deckbox until the link is cleared or the Deckbox is removed.
If the Deckbox is broken while locked, the Deck Control will not automatically relink to a new one.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.linking.note: In the GUI header you’ll see “Linked: ✓” when it has a valid Deckbox link.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.redstone_draw: A redstone pulse will draw the top card and eject it from the front face.
There is a short cooldown to prevent rapid-fire pulses.
The ejected card goes in the block’s facing direction.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.selecting.bul: Click a card in your player inventory to select it.
The left panel shows the selected card art + its Mana Value (MV).
Cascade uses the selected card’s MV as the source MV.
Draw: removes the top card and ejects it.
Shuffle: randomizes the library order (without moving items around in the Deckbox slots).
Peek N: privately shows the top N cards (only you can see the overlay).
Scry: look at N, drag to reorder, choose what stays on top vs goes to bottom.
Surveil: look at N, drag cards to keep on top vs mill into the graveyard.
Mill: removes the top N cards; tries to insert into an adjacent Graveyard, otherwise ejects out the back.
Peek N opens a private overlay that shows the top cards. Click “Done” to close. No cards are moved—this is view-only.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.scry_surveil_: Click and drag cards between the two rows.
Scry: Top row = stays on top of the library. Bottom row = goes to bottom.
Surveil: Top row = stays on top. Bottom row = goes to Graveyard (milled).
Confirm applies the result. Cancel closes without applying.
Tip: You can move cards into exact order in the top row. The top row order becomes the new top of the library.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.place_selecte: Opens an overlay to insert the selected card into the library.
From top #: place at a specific depth (1 = top card).
Place uses 1 card from the selected stack in your inventory. The library must have an empty slot available in the Deckbox.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.cascade.title: Cascade
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.cascade.bulle: Select a card (source MV), then press Start Cascade.
The block reveals cards from the top until it finds a nonland with MV < source MV.
You choose: Cast (eject the hit) or Exile (don’t eject it).
All revealed cards that weren’t ejected are placed on the bottom in a randomized order.
Cancel behaves like Exile (it bottoms everything).
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.gy_reset.bull: Shuffle GY → Library: pulls Graveyard cards and inserts them into the Deckbox, then shuffles.
Reset Deck: pulls Graveyard + Exile (more slots), inserts into the Deckbox, then shuffles.
If the Deckbox is full, leftovers eject out the back.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.notes.title: Notes & behavior details
Deck Control tracks an internal library order so it can “shuffle” without physically rearranging Deckbox slots.
If the Deckbox contents change, the order is reconciled/rebuilt automatically (debounced).
Mill/Surveil will try to insert into a nearby Graveyard; if none is present, items eject out the back.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.variants.body: Deck Control comes in multiple decorative variants so you can match different build palettes.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.variants.bull: All variants behave the same — the difference is purely visual.
Pick the one that fits your base: stone, polished granite/diorite/andesite, polished tuff/deepslate, polished blackstone, prismarine.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.window.title: Window controls (items)
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.window.body: Right-click the Deck Control with certain items to change the window style. This does not open the GUI.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.window.bullet: Empty hand: opens the Deck Control GUI.
Sneak + empty hand: shuffles the library.
Shovel: turns the window off (unlit). Flint & Steel or Fire Charge: turns it back on.
Window color: Netherrack = default, Soul Sand = blue, Redstone = red, Copper Nugget = green.
guide.mtgcard.deck_control.window.note: Tip: Because the GUI only opens with an empty main hand, you won’t accidentally pop the UI while holding building blocks.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.title: Health Tracker
guide.mtgcard.life_point.p_overview: The Health Tracker is an in-world life tracker for MTG-style games. It stores life, commander damage, custom counters, and pod (group) game state.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_open_right_cl: Right-click the block to open the Life Point screen.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_open_name_fie: Use the Name field at the top to set your display name.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_open_tabs: Tabs: Life, Counters, Pods, and Edit.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_life_type_to_: Click the big life number and type to set it directly.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_life_scroll: Scroll on the life number to change life by ±1 (Shift = ±10).
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_life_counters: Counters appear below your life panel. Hover a counter and scroll to change its value.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_cmd_select_ta: Pick an opponent from the Other Players list to edit commander damage.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_cmd_edit_meth: Edit using typing, +/- buttons, or scrolling over the field.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_cmd_updates_l: Commander damage updates your life total automatically (damage taken = life lost).
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_cmd_lethal_wa: When damage reaches lethal, the field highlights as a warning.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_ctr_add_custo: Add custom counters using “+ Add Counter”.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_ctr_edit_valu: Set counter values by typing or scrolling (Shift = ±10).
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_ctr_icons: Assign an icon to each counter using the icon picker.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_ctr_builtin: Poison, Energy, and Experience are always available as built-in counters.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_pod_create_se: Create a pod with “+ Create”, then select it to edit.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_pod_scan_near: The screen scans for nearby Life Point blocks to add to your pod.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_pod_add_remov: Add/remove members by clicking them (max 6 members).
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_pod_save_dele: Rename and save the pod, or delete it from the Pods tab.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_pod_locked_me: If a block is locked in another pod, remove it from that pod before adding it here.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_game_start: Start begins the pod game and locks in turn order.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_game_pass: Pass is only available to the active player and advances the turn.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_game_reset: Reset clears the pod game state.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_game_dead_ali: Dead/Alive marks a player as dead so they can be skipped.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_rs_comparator: Comparator outputs 15 when this block is the active player, otherwise 0.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_rs_pulse_pass: A rising-edge redstone pulse will pass the turn if this block is currently active.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_rs_automation: Tip: combine comparator output + pulse logic for turn automation.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_edit_colors: Customize Player Color and Life Color (palette or hex).
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_edit_format: Choose a display format: Commander, Standard, Brawl, or Two-Headed.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_edit_icon_and: Pick an icon and optionally recolor red areas using Icon Swap Color.
guide.mtgcard.life_point.b_edit_presets: Save presets and apply them later for quick style changes.
guide.mtgcard.display.title: Display Screen
guide.mtgcard.display.p_overview: The Display Screen block is a wall screen that shows a linked Life Point player: life total, name, color styling, and optional overlays like commander damage.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_link_sneak_use_i: Sneak-right-click a Life Point block while holding the Display item to bind it.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_link_sound: A short “pling” sound confirms the item was linked.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_link_persists_it: The link is stored on the item and carries over when you place the block.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_place_applies_li: When placed, the Display block reads the link from the item and binds itself automatically.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_place_inherit_fr: Unlinked Display blocks can inherit a link from adjacent Display blocks with the same facing.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_place_propagates: A linked Display can propagate its link across a connected component to “claim” nearby unlinked tiles.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_multi_same_facin: Display blocks merge into one screen only when they share the same facing/orientation.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_multi_same_link_: A screen only merges tiles that are linked to the same Life Point. Different links create hard boundaries.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_multi_largest_re: The renderer uses the largest filled rectangle inside the connected tiles. Extra tiles outside the rectangle render as small 1×1 screens.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_multi_controller: Only the controller tile renders the screen to prevent duplicate drawing and flicker.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_render_same_dime: Displays only render if the linked Life Point is in the same dimension as the client.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_render_turn_pip: When it’s that player’s turn, a small colored pip appears in the top corner.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_render_dead_skul: If the player is marked dead in their pod, the screen swaps to a skull state.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_render_icon_swap: If the player uses an icon with red areas, the screen recolors those pixels using the Icon Swap Color.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_render_commander: Commander damage bubbles only appear on larger screens (minimum area required) and are hidden while dead.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_update_controlle: The controller periodically syncs the linked Life Point state to nearby tracking players.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_update_missing_l: If the linked Life Point block no longer exists (or is unloaded), the Display clears its link automatically.
guide.mtgcard.display.b_update_no_chunk_: Displays never load chunks or dimensions just to resolve a link, keeping servers safe from forced chunk loads.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.title: Graveyard
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.p_overview: The Graveyard block is a two-sided card container: a 10×10 Graveyard and a 10×10 Exile. It’s designed for fast sorting and quick mass moves during games.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_two_grids: Contains two 10×10 grids: Graveyard (left) and Exile (right).
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_card_only: Only MTG Card items can be stored in either side.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_open_state: The block visually opens while players have the UI open.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_exile_all: Exile All moves every card from Graveyard → Exile, filling empty slots first.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_return_all: Return All moves every card from Exile → Graveyard, filling empty slots first.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_overflow_eject: If the destination side is full, leftover cards are ejected out the back of the block.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_preview_cards_: Hovering a card slot shows a large art preview for that card.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_preview_deboun: Previews have a short hover delay to prevent flicker while moving the mouse.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_preview_foil_s: Foil cards show a shimmering sweep effect in the preview.
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_hopper_insert_: Hoppers can insert cards, but only into the Graveyard side (not Exile).
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_hopper_extract: Hopper extraction is blocked (cards won’t be pulled out automatically).
guide.mtgcard.graveyard.b_comparator_upd: Comparator output updates when the inventory changes.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.title: Card Store
guide.mtgcard.card_store.p_overview: The Card Store is a fullscreen terminal for searching and buying printed cards. Add prints to your cart, pay with the configured currency item, and the store will "print" and deliver your order over time.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_search: Type a search and press Enter to load results.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_scryfall_synt: Advanced searches support Scryfall-style syntax (example: set:neo t:dragon).
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_results_grid: Results appear in a grid that automatically sizes to your screen (more space = more results per page).
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_sorting: Sort results by Scryfall Order, Set/Number, Name, Price, Set, or Collector Number.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_preview: Selecting a card shows a large preview panel with its current cost.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_cart_add: Use Add to Cart to collect prints you want to buy.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_cart_qty: Adjust quantities with the + / - buttons on each cart line.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_cart_total: The right panel shows your total cost and the currency basis.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_cart_buy: Press Buy to confirm the cart (Buy is disabled if you can’t afford it).
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_printing_tick: Orders print one card at a time with a short delay between prints.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_deliver_deckb: Printed cards try to insert into any adjacent Deckbox first.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_eject_front: If no adjacent Deckbox has room, the card is ejected out the front of the store.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_break_flush: If the store is broken while printing, all remaining cards are flushed out the front.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_drag_drop: Drag and drop .txt or .csv deck files into the screen to import directly into your cart.
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_txt_format: TXT format supports lines like: 1x Card Name (SET) 123
guide.mtgcard.card_store.b_csv_format: CSV format supports header-based columns, or common sheet layouts that include set code and collector number.
guide.mtgcard.commands.title: Commands
guide.mtgcard.commands.p_overview: MtgCard provides several commands for managing card art, custom cards, and decks. These are primarily utility and power-user tools.
guide.mtgcard.commands.p_art: Commands for managing downloaded and cached card artwork.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_art_root: /mtg art — Base command for all art-related actions. This will show the total amount of art saved in the world.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_art_find: /mtg art find <id> — Locate a specific art key.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_art_purge: /mtg art purge — Clears all cached card art. It will avoid all custom card art.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_art_rebuild: /mtg art rebuild — Rebuilds the art cache from available sources.
guide.mtgcard.commands.p_custom: Commands for creating, importing, and managing custom cards and sets.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_custom_card: /mtg custom card <name> — Gives data on that custom card
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_custom_import: /mtg custom import — Import custom cards from external data.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_custom_remove_c: /mtg custom remove card <name> — Remove a specific custom card.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_custom_remove_s: /mtg custom remove set <set> — Remove an entire custom set.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_custom_sets: /mtg custom sets — List all installed custom sets.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_deck_list: /mtg deck list — Lists all exported decks.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_deck_export: /mtg deck export <name> — Exports a deck for sharing or backup. Will be exported as a .txt and a .csv file.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_tips_permission: Some commands may require operator permissions.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_tips_server: On servers, run commands on the side that owns the data you are modifying.
guide.mtgcard.commands.b_tips_troublesho: If card art is missing or incorrect, try purging and rebuilding the art cache.
guide.mtgcard.home.title: Welcome
guide.mtgcard.home.p_what: MtgCard brings Magic: The Gathering–style cards into Minecraft as physical, interactive objects. Cards can be collected, displayed, traded, and used as part of your world — not just stored in menus.
guide.mtgcard.home.p_smp: MtgCard is designed with multiplayer servers in mind, encouraging interaction, specialization, and long-term progression.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_smp_economy: Supports player-driven economies through packs, singles, and custom cards.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_smp_trading: Cards are tangible items that can be traded, gifted, stolen, or displayed.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_smp_social: Life tracking, displays, and shared spaces make games and events visible to others.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_design_builders: Blocks are designed to look good in builds, not just serve a function.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_design_survival: Everything fits naturally into survival gameplay and progression.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_design_modular: Systems are modular — use as much or as little of the mod as you want.
guide.mtgcard.home.p_guide: This guidebook walks through every major system in the mod, organized for both new players and power users.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_nav_categories: Use the tabs on the left to switch between categories.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_nav_chapters: Each category contains focused chapters for specific blocks, items, or systems.
guide.mtgcard.home.b_nav_progression: Start here, then explore Blocks and Items as you encounter them in-game.
guide.mtgcard.config.title: Config
guide.mtgcard.config.p_location: MtgCard uses a TOML config file in your Minecraft config folder.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_location_legacy: Legacy migration: if config/mtgcard.json exists, it will be read once and converted into mtgcard.toml.
guide.mtgcard.config.p_import: Controls who is allowed to import custom cards into the world/server.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_import_anyone: import.anyone_can_import: If true, any player can use the importer.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_import_whitelist: import.whitelist: If anyone_can_import is false, only these usernames can import.
guide.mtgcard.config.p_cards: Controls how downloaded cards are requested from Scryfall.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_cards_language: cards.language: Preferred Scryfall language code (falls back to English if unavailable).
guide.mtgcard.config.b_cards_language_ex: Examples: en, es, fr, de, it, pt, ja, ko, ru, zhs, zht
guide.mtgcard.config.p_pack: Custom card chances are per-slot and range from 0.0 to 1.0 (0.10 = 10%).
guide.mtgcard.config.b_pack_common: pack.custom_chances.common: Chance for a custom COMMON.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_pack_uncommon: pack.custom_chances.uncommon: Chance for a custom UNCOMMON.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_pack_wildcard: pack.custom_chances.wildcard_c_or_u: Chance for a custom wildcard (common/uncommon).
guide.mtgcard.config.b_pack_rare: pack.custom_chances.rare_or_mythic: Chance for a custom RARE/MYTHIC.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_pack_random: pack.custom_chances.random: Chance for a custom random card.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_pack_foil: pack.custom_chances.random_foil: Chance for a custom random FOIL card.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_pack_basic: pack.custom_chances.basic_land: Chance for a custom basic land.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_pack_token: pack.custom_chances.token_or_art: Chance for a custom token/art slot.
guide.mtgcard.config.p_pack_note: Note: These values affect pack generation globally. They do not change official set odds — they only control the chance that a slot pulls from your custom pool instead.
guide.mtgcard.config.p_price: Controls how the card prices are to be used on the server with the card store.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_price_item: price.item: Item id used as the price icon (example: minecraft:diamond).
guide.mtgcard.config.b_price_basis: price.basis: Which Scryfall price to show: USD, EUR, or TIX.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_tips_restart: Most config changes are easiest to apply with a game/server restart.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_tips_servers: On servers, the server config controls pack/custom-card behavior for everyone.
guide.mtgcard.config.b_tips_ranges: Chances are clamped to 0..1, and invalid language codes fall back to English.
advancement.mtgcard.root.title: MTG Card
advancement.mtgcard.root.description: Open packs, collect cards, and build your setup.
